latest_release.name: v0.6.0
latest_release.body:
## Summary

ARTEX v0.6.0 makes a finding provable, hardens the agents against the content they read, and adds an opt-in approval gate for targets. The target gate ships OFF by default and through the API only, so existing deployments keep their current behavior after upgrading.

Full list: [CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/BaaRai/ARTEX/blob/v0.6.0/CHANGELOG.md) · [compare v0.5.1...v0.6.0](https://github.com/BaaRai/ARTEX/compare/v0.5.1...v0.6.0)

## Highlights

- **Verified findings (S1)**: findings carry a POE level and a verification status. `verified` requires a bound proof or verification response, a declared POE level of 3 or more, and every evidence quote of 8 runes or more found verbatim in a bound body. A retest verdict can upgrade a finding, and the findings UI shows the badge, the filter and the note (#162, #163, #164, #169).
- **Target gate (S3b phase 1 and step 2.1)**: opt-in per task or conversation, API only, OFF by default. Approvals pin `host:port` and the resolved IPs. WebFetch and direct custom `http` calls connect only to pinned or exempt addresses on every redirect hop, with no direct retry in a gated scope (#177 to #186).
- **Agentic hardening (#124)**: code-owned untrusted-content rules for the planner and the compactor, a planner goal anchor, `goal_met` and `prove_goal` guards, truthful hint origins, and the `[built-in]` deny rules applied to the planner and main-agent Bash (#189, #190).
- **Intercept audit**: approvals record `decided_by`, and the `[model]`/`[Model]` prefix bug no longer stores judge decisions as `unknown` (#159, #165).
- **Notifications**: configurable summary and asset limits, plus Feishu digest overflow handling (#170 to #174).
- **Docker supply chain**: recon tools verified against their release checksums, sqlmap pinned to tag 1.9.9 at a fixed commit, Node 22.23.4 verified against `SHASUMS256.txt`, and the Playwright packages pinned (#188).
- **Intent claim leases**: a heartbeat, a TTL and an owner token stop a stale worker from overwriting a result (#176).
- **Smaller fixes**: custom User-Agent per LLM profile, the custom-tool proxy scheme fix, and the `list_task_credentials` schema fix (#155, #187, #130).

## Upgrade notes

- **No manual migration**: schema changes are idempotent at startup. Existing findings stay `unverified`, and the new optional fields default to empty.
- **The target gate is off by default**. With it off, behavior is unchanged. With it on, an uncovered target waits for an approval.
- **`goal_met` refuses while a goal is open**, and `prove_goal` accepts a fact only with `confidence=observed`.
- **The planner and the main agent now run the `[built-in]` deny rules** (destructive commands, delete-style endpoints). User rules and the judge still do not apply to them.
- **Findings gain `counterevidence` and `confidence_rationale`**, optional and never blocking. Existing databases receive the schema property at startup.
- **0.5.x is no longer supported.** Fixes target the latest release line only; upgrade to 0.6.0.

## Known limits

- The target gate reads the targets a call declares. A subprocess that builds its target at run time is not seen, and a call through a proxy is not bound yet (recording-proxy binding is step 2.2).
- URL rules match the URL as written, with no normalization; use a domain, IP or CIDR rule to keep an agent away from a host.
- Fact provenance arrives in 0.7.0. Until then, `prove_goal` trusts the `confidence` the model declared.
- The new `add_hint` and `prove_goal` tool descriptions reach fresh databases only; the server-side refusals apply everywhere.
- The prompt rules are advisory to the model. The enforced parts are the `goal_met`/`prove_goal` handlers, the built-in deny rules and the target gate.
- No Docker image is published for this release. Build from the checkout with `docker compose up -d --build`, or use a binary from the assets below.

## Contributors

- @kiserufetch: thank you for the `list_task_credentials` schema fix (#130).
-

# ARTEX **Autonomous penetration testing that keeps its receipts.** (upstream: [Autumn-27/ARTEX](https://github.com/Autumn-27), AGPL-3.0) Self-hosted multi-agent offensive security. A planner explores, workers run real tools, and every finding stays bound to the assets and HTTP traffic that prove it. [![Release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/BaaRai/ARTEX?label=release&color=6b34db)](https://github.com/BaaRai/ARTEX/releases) [![License](https://img.shields.io/github/license/BaaRai/ARTEX?color=6b34db)](LICENSE) [![CI](https://github.com/BaaRai/ARTEX/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg?branch=main)](https://github.com/BaaRai/ARTEX/actions/workflows/ci.yml) [![Go](https://img.shields.io/github/go-mod/go-version/BaaRai/ARTEX?color=6b34db)](go.mod) [Quick start](#quick-start) · [Screenshots](#screenshots) · [How it works](#how-it-works) · [Install](#installation) · [Configuration](#configuration) · [Security](SECURITY.md)
--- ARTEX is a self-hosted, LLM-driven penetration testing platform. It is not a chat wrapper around a scanner: a planner splits a goal into intents, workers execute them with real tools, and the results are written back into **two linked graphs**: one for what you know about the target, one for how the test is progressing. Every finding can carry the captured request and response that justify it, and every autonomous action passes through scope rules, approval gates and budgets. - **It explores, it doesn't chat.** Goal decomposition, intent dispatch, worker execution and write-back form a closed loop that keeps advancing until the goal is proven. - **Two graphs, one audit trail.** The shared asset graph says *what exists*; the per-task exploration graph says *what was tried, what it produced, and why*. Anchors link the two. - **Findings with evidence.** A recording MITM proxy and a browser extension capture real traffic; findings, evidence quotes and retests are tied to the exact request/response. - **Autonomy with brakes.** Human-in-the-loop approvals, argv-prefix rules, scope/deny gates, token and turn budgets, a target noise governor, and prompt-injection framing on tool output. - **Self-hosted and model-agnostic.** One Go binary with the Next.js UI embedded, PostgreSQL, your own Anthropic/OpenAI-compatible endpoint, or a local Ollama. --- ## Quick start ```bash git clone https://github.com/BaaRai/ARTEX.git cd ARTEX cp .env.example .env # set POSTGRES_PASSWORD (and optionally an LLM key) docker compose up -d --build # builds from this checkout, starts PostgreSQL ``` Open **http://localhost:8787**. On the first visit `/setup` asks for the one-time setup token printed at startup: ```bash docker compose logs artex | grep "Setup token" ``` > There is no prebuilt Docker image to pull: the image is always built from your checkout. > For all installation paths (script, binaries, source, release archives), see [Installation](#installation). --- ## Multi-provider workers In **System → LLM**, configure the profiles you want to use. In **System → Settings**, set the concurrent worker count to at least **2** before starting a task (the count applies to subsequently started tasks). In **System → Agents → Worker**, leave the model set to follow the task; a fixed Worker model takes precedence over rotation. When creating a task, select both profiles in **LLM config chain**, arrange their order, and enable **Enable multi-LLM worker rotation**. For an existing task, open its LLM config control, change the switch or profile order, and save. Rotation assigns successive worker intents A, B, A, B, regardless of completion order. Separate intents can run concurrently on different providers; each intent keeps its selected provider unless it fails over. Planner and other unbound roles continue using the task's current profile. Turning rotation off restores ordered task-level failover. An excluded provider is skipped, so an intent pinned to an exhausted profile falls back to the task's current profile instead of retrying it; rotation keeps cycling the whole list and does not rebalance around a dead provider. Saving the chain resets their failure state. Changes do not interrupt in-flight calls. The rotation cursor starts again after a server restart and saving the chain does not reset it; the profile order and switch remain persisted. The task creation and `PUT /api/tasks/{id}/llm` APIs accept `llm_rotate: true` alongside the ordered `llm_profile_ids`. Omitting `llm_rotate` on an update preserves its value. ## Screenshots | Tasks | Findings | | :---: | :---: | | ![Tasks](screenshots/tasks.png) | ![Findings](screenshots/findings.png) | | Task execution: sessions and tool calls | Exploration graph | | :---: | :---: | | ![Execution](screenshots/sessions.png) | ![Exploration graph](screenshots/graph.png) | | Asset coverage graph | Traffic recording | | :---: | :---: | | ![Asset coverage graph](screenshots/assets_test.png) | ![Traffic](screenshots/traffic.png) | | Human-in-the-loop chat | Interception approvals | | :---: | :---: | | ![Chat](screenshots/chat.png) | ![Interception](screenshots/intercept.png) |
More screenshots (assets, agents, LLM, logs) | Assets | Agent management | | :---: | :---: | | ![Assets](screenshots/assets.png) | ![Agent](screenshots/agents.png) | | LLM configuration | Backend logs | | :---: | :---: | | ![LLM](screenshots/llm.png) | ![Logs](screenshots/logs.png) |
--- ## How it works ### Dual-graph architecture: exploration graph + asset graph ARTEX separates *what the goals are* from *how far testing has progressed* into two independent graphs linked by anchors: - **Asset graph (shared across tasks).** One source of truth for `root_domain / subdomain / ip / service / app / endpoint`, owned by companies. Parent-child relationships and deduplication keys are computed by the program; agents only submit raw observations. - **Exploration graph (per task).** The task's reasoning and progress: `goal / intent / fact / finding / hint` nodes connected by `spawns / derived_from / yields / proves` edges into a lineage chain. - **Anchors link them.** `exploration_anchors(node_id, asset_id)` ties intents, facts and findings to concrete assets: which assets a direction touched, and which intents tested a given asset. This also powers **asset test coverage** and the coverage graph. ```mermaid flowchart LR subgraph EG["Exploration graph (per-task · advance chain)"] direction TB G["goal"] I1["intent A"] F1["fact"] I2["intent B"] FD["finding (vulnerability)"] G -->|spawns| I1 I1 -->|yields| F1 F1 -->|derived_from| I2 I2 -->|proves| FD end subgraph AG["Asset graph (globally shared · source of truth)"] direction TB RD["root_domain"] SD["subdomain"] SV["service"] EP["endpoint"] RD --> SD --> SV --> EP end I1 -. anchor .-> SD F1 -. anchor .-> SV I2 -. anchor .-> EP FD -. anchor .-> EP ``` The **planner** reads the exploration graph, judges goals, and dispatches intents only when there is an uncovered direction; a **worker** claims one intent, executes it, writes assets/facts/findings back into both graphs, then stops. ### The engine loop The engine is event-driven: any graph change wakes the planner, workers claim and execute intents, write-back triggers the next round, until `prove_goal` closes the task. ```mermaid sequenceDiagram autonumber participant EV as graph-change debounce participant P as planner participant FR as frontier intent queue participant W as worker participant PX as recording proxy participant DB as dual graphs + activity EV-->>P: wake up P->>DB: read situation (graph_overview prefetch + coverage/scope) P->>FR: dispatch 0..N intents (with asset_ids) Note over P,FR: most wake-ups dispatch 0 (no new direction means done) W->>FR: claimNext claims one intent W->>DB: fetch the raw assets of the intent's asset_ids W->>PX: real tool execution (Kali / Bash / HTTP) PX-->>W: response (fully traced + CA verified) W->>DB: write back fact / asset / finding + per-step activity DB-->>EV: graph change EV-->>P: wake again (closed loop) ``` ### Durable attack chains, shared worker memory Real attack chains are multi-step and ordered (find an injection → get credentials → move laterally). The planner keeps a **todolist retained per task across wake-ups**: it records the chain once, then dispatches the next step only when its prerequisites are satisfied by facts. Workers can also **search each other's execution traces** (`search_all_worker_traces`, `list_worker_traces`, `get_worker_trace`). Observations that never became formal facts (an error message, a response snippet, a hidden parameter) are still reusable by the next worker, while each worker remains confined to the intent it claimed. --- ## Features ### Evidence, not chat logs - **Recording MITM proxy** (`:8788`) with a generated CA: every Bash/HTTP tool call is traced, and request/response evidence can be bound to a finding. - **Browser extension** (`extension/`) for authenticated targets: log in once (captcha, email OTP, 2FA included), capture the session, and the requests/responses land in the same traffic store.
Using the traffic capture extension - Load the unpacked extension from `extension/` (Chrome/Edge: Developer Mode → Load unpacked); - In the popup, set your ARTEX URL and token, then press **Start capture** on the tab you are browsing; - Use the site normally; text requests/responses are batched to `POST /api/traffic/ingest` (authenticated). Binary bodies (images, fonts) are skipped, bodies are truncated at 256 KiB, batches are capped at 50 entries; - Press **Stop** when done. Everything stays in your local traffic store.
- **Verified findings**: findings carry a POE level, a verification status and a note; a finding is `verified` only when a bound proof/response and verbatim evidence quotes support it. Gzip/deflate bodies are decoded before the quote check. - **Vulnerability retest loop**: a dedicated `retester` agent re-runs a finding with optional fixed version/conditions, records `Still reproducible / Fixed / Cannot confirm`, and can move the finding to `Fixed` automatically. Original evidence and reports are preserved. - **Reports and exports**: findings, evidence and task archives, with traffic snapshots kept encrypted at rest. ### Control without slowing down - **Interception gate**: every tool call can require human approval, with rules by `string`, `regex` or **argv prefix**. An argv rule is a JSON array of 1 to 8 tokens (Bash only, for example `["git","push"]`); it matches only a single simple command whose parsed prefix equals the pattern exactly. Pipes, lists, redirections, prefix assignments, subshells, background jobs, wrapper programs and command/parameter substitutions do not match; flags are ignored by construction (`["git","push"]` covers `git push --force`, but `git -C /repo push` matches nothing). Each approval records who decided: `human`, `rule`, `model` or `system`. - **Scope and target gate**: scope rows define the coverage denominator; assets outside the declared scope are not explored. The target gate (off by default, API-only) can refuse destinations that were not approved. - **Budgets**: `ARTEX_TASK_BUDGET_TOKENS` / `ARTEX_TASK_BUDGET_TURNS` cap a whole task (planner and workers); `ARTEX_INTENT_BUDGET_TOKENS` / `ARTEX_INTENT_BUDGET_TURNS` cap one worker run. Near the limit the task enters a forced wrap-up; a worker is not started when the remaining budget cannot cover it. Budgets are in memory: a restart starts fresh. - **Noise governor**: `ARTEX_NOISE_PROFILE=quiet|balanced|aggressive` paces requests ARTEX sends to targets (per-host rate, burst, in-flight limit, jitter, backoff on 429/503, short GET caching). With a profile set, agents also receive low-and-slow flags for the installed scanners. - **Untrusted-output boundary (on by default)**: tool results are framed between nonce-tagged markers so the model treats them as data, not instructions. Disable with `ARTEX_UNTRUSTED_BOUNDARY=0`. ### Assets and coverage - **Coverage ledger and force-directed coverage graph**: in-scope assets are highlighted as tested or untested, with linked intents, facts and findings per node. - **Company-scoped asset graph**: shared across tasks, deduplicated by the program, with domain → subdomain → service → endpoint containment. - **ScopeSentry sync**: pull asset data from a [ScopeSentry](https://github.com/Autumn-27/ScopeSentry) instance by project or task, merged by company scope into the asset graph for agents to explore.
Syncing from ScopeSentry - On the **Asset Sync** page, enter the ScopeSentry address and API key; - Choose the targets and asset types by **project** or **task** (domains / subdomains / IPs / ports / sites / endpoints…); - Import: rows are merged by company asset scope and become part of the asset graph.
- **Task categories, templates, relations and archives** for repeatable engagements. ### Platform - **LLM profiles with failover**: Anthropic, OpenAI, OpenAI-compatible relays and keyless Ollama; multiple profiles per task with automatic failover. - **Token accounting**: per-task and per-session usage, cache reads/writes, and an LLM record view for every call. - **MCP servers, skills, memory and a workspace**: extend the agent with remote tools and reusable prompt/playbook material. - **Single binary**: the Next.js UI is embedded with `go:embed`; PostgreSQL is the only external dependency. --- ## Installation > Requires **PostgreSQL**; exploration requires an **LLM** (`ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` or > `OPENAI_API_KEY`, also configurable in the UI). ### Option 1: one-click install script (recommended) ```bash git clone https://github.com/BaaRai/ARTEX.git cd ARTEX ./install.sh ``` The script detects or installs Docker, then offers **① all-Docker** (writes `.env`, runs `docker compose up -d --build`) or **② local build and run** (generates `config.json`, builds the embedded binary, starts it). Open **http://localhost:8787**; `/setup` asks for the one-time setup token printed at startup (`docker compose logs artex | grep "Setup token"`). The UI listens on `127.0.0.1` by default. To reach it from another machine (or from Windows when ARTEX runs inside WSL), set `ARTEX_BIND_ADDR=0.0.0.0` in `.env` (the setup token still protects the first-run claim), or keep loopback and use a reverse proxy or SSH tunnel. ### Option 2: Docker Compose (manual) ```bash git clone https://github.com/BaaRai/ARTEX.git cd ARTEX cp .env.example .env # set POSTGRES_PASSWORD, optionally ANTHROPIC_API_KEY docker compose up -d --build # → http://localhost:8787 ``` The image includes a scanner toolchain (`nmap`, `nuclei`, `httpx`, `katana`, `ffuf`, `dalfox`, `sqlmap`, `ripgrep`, `curl`, `npm`, …); `./skills` and `./data` are persisted via bind mounts. For remote MCP you can choose `http` (Streamable HTTP) or `sse` (legacy SSE) in system settings. Legacy SSE servers usually establish the event stream with `GET /sse` and receive JSON-RPC over `/message?sessionId=...`; configure the URL as `/sse` and send `Authorization: Bearer `. ### Option 3: prebuilt binaries (Releases) Download the zip for your platform from [Releases](https://github.com/BaaRai/ARTEX/releases). It contains `artex`, `start.sh` (`start.bat` on Windows), `skills/` and `config.example.json`: ```bash cp config.example.json config.json # fill in the database connection ./start.sh # → http://localhost:8787 ``` Start with `start.sh` / `start.bat`, not `./artex`: it is a daemon script that restarts the process after a backoff. To keep it in the background: `nohup ./start.sh >artex.log 2>&1 &`. #### Verifying a release Each release attaches `SHA256SUMS` and a CycloneDX SBOM, `artex-.cdx.json` (Go modules in the linux/amd64 binary, the frontend `package-lock.json`, `go.mod`/`go.sum`), next to the zips. The zips also carry a GitHub build provenance attestation. Releases published before this was added have neither. ```bash sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS # add --ignore-missing if you downloaded only some zips gh attestation verify --repo BaaRai/ARTEX # built by this repository's release workflow ``` ### Option 4: build the single binary from source ```bash cd web && npm ci && npm run build:static && cd .. cp -r web/out server/webui/dist CGO_ENABLED=0 go build -tags embedui -o artex ./cmd/artex ./start.sh ``` Only `-tags embedui` embeds the frontend into the binary. ### Option 5: cross-platform release archives `build.sh` builds and embeds the frontend, strips debug info, and writes zips for Linux amd64/arm64, macOS amd64/arm64 and Windows amd64 by default: ```bash ./build.sh --release # output: dist/artex--*.zip ARTEX_TARGETS=linux/amd64,windows/amd64 ./build.sh --release ./build.sh --target linux/amd64 --upx ``` UPX is disabled by default: self-extracting binaries may be incompatible with some kernels, virtualization environments or security policies. Pass `--upx` only after confirming the target runtime supports it. --- ## Configuration **Database** (`config.json`, or the `ARTEX_PG_DSN` environment variable): ```json { "database": { "host": "127.0.0.1", "port": 5432, "user": "artex", "password": "yourpass", "dbname": "artex", "sslmode": "disable" } } ``` **LLM**: `export ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=sk-...` (or `OPENAI_API_KEY`), or configure it in the UI's "LLM Configuration" page, which can also add a local Ollama server as a keyless provider (format "Ollama", default base URL `http://127.0.0.1:11434/v1`). Optional: `ARTEX_LLM_PROVIDER` (`anthropic | openai | openai-responses | ollama`), `ARTEX_LLM_MODEL`, `ARTEX_LLM_BASE_URL`, `ARTEX_LLM_PROXY`. **Base URL gotcha**: for the Anthropic format, enter the host **without** `/v1` (for example `https://api.anthropic.com`); ARTEX appends `/v1/messages`. OpenAI-format providers append `/chat/completions` (or `/responses` for `openai-responses`), so their base **does** end in `/v1` (for example `https://api.openai.com/v1`). **Concurrency**: work agents per task, in "System Settings" (default 3). **Untrusted-output boundary (on by default)**: tool results for the worker, planner, chat and main agent are framed between nonce-tagged markers so the model treats them as data, not instructions. Unset or empty, the boundary is on; set `ARTEX_UNTRUSTED_BOUNDARY=0` (or `false` / `off` / `no`) to disable it. Cost: about 154 bytes per tool result plus one system note. **Noise profile (off by default)**: `ARTEX_NOISE_PROFILE` paces the requests ARTEX sends to targets (WebFetch, HTTP custom tools, the enrich probe). Unset or `off` keeps today's behaviour: no limit, no cache. `quiet` = 2 req/s per host (burst 4, 1 in flight), `balanced` = 5 req/s (burst 10, 2 in flight), `aggressive` = 20 req/s (burst 40, 4 in flight). A profile adds jitter, backs off on 429/503 (honours `Retry-After`, bounded retries, GET/HEAD/OPTIONS only), deduplicates identical in-flight GETs and caches them briefly (60/30/10 s; never POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE), and logs a per-host noise line each minute. `ARTEX_TARGET_USER_AGENT` sets a User-Agent on target requests that carry none. With traffic capture on, Bash commands that use the proxy (curl, wget, python-requests) are paced too, per host by the same rate and jitter, and counted in the same per-host lines. The in-flight caps, retries and cache apply only to ARTEX's own requests. This is best effort, not a security boundary. Raw scanners such as nmap are not paced, and neither is a command that bypasses the proxy (`--noproxy`, a removed proxy variable). With capture off, nothing launched from Bash is paced. The low-and-slow prompt block supplies the rate flags in every case. The **Target noise** card in System settings sets the profile at runtime (no restart) and shows the per-host counters; once saved, that setting takes precedence over `ARTEX_NOISE_PROFILE`. **Low-and-slow agent guidance (off by default)**: when a noise profile is set, the planner, worker, main agent and chat agents receive a code-owned prompt block with the profile's per-host limits and exact rate/delay flags for the installed scanners. It tells them to test one host at a time, back off on 429/503 and never raise the rate to meet a deadline. **Run budgets (off by default)**: `ARTEX_TASK_BUDGET_TOKENS` / `ARTEX_TASK_BUDGET_TURNS` cap a task's total spend (planner rounds and workers); `ARTEX_INTENT_BUDGET_TOKENS` / `ARTEX_INTENT_BUDGET_TURNS` cap one worker run. Unset or `0` means unlimited. A worker is not started when the remaining task budget cannot cover its estimated cost (the average of finished workers, else 50,000 tokens and 10 turns). Near the wrap-up reserve (the larger of 5% and 20,000 tokens, and 2 turns) the task enters a forced wrap-up: the planner writes a summary and final goal judgment, and workers may only write back. The task then ends `done` if its goals are met, else `timeout`. Practical floor: below 50,000 tokens no worker starts; 50,000-70,000 typically gives one worker then wrap-up; pick well above 70,000 for real exploration. **Common flags**: `./start.sh -addr :8787 -proxy :8788` (`-addr` frontend/API, `-proxy` traffic recording proxy). ### Reverse proxy deployment (HTTPS / exposing only 443) The frontend, API and SSE stream share port 8787 (the binary listens on `127.0.0.1:8787` by default; the Docker container publishes on `127.0.0.1`), and the activity stream is same-origin by default, so **no `NEXT_PUBLIC_SSE_BASE` is needed**: expose 443 and keep 8787 internal. SSE keeps a long-lived connection with continuous pushes, so the proxy **must disable buffering**; otherwise the browser connects but never receives events. Nginx example: ```nginx server { listen 443 ssl; server_name your.domain.com; # ssl_certificate / ssl_certificate_key ... location / { proxy_pass http://127.0.0.1:8787; proxy_set_header Host $host; proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-Proto $scheme; proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-For $proxy_add_x_forwarded_for; # SSE essentials: buffering off, long timeouts, HTTP/1.1 proxy_buffering off; proxy_cache off; proxy_read_timeout 3600s; proxy_http_version 1.1; proxy_set_header Connection ""; } } ``` **Login rate limit behind a proxy**: login allows 10 attempts per minute per client IP. Behind a proxy every request comes from the proxy's address, so without further setup all users share one budget and an attacker who fails 10 logins blocks everyone, admin included, for up to 15 minutes. Keep the `X-Forwarded-For` line and set `ARTEX_TRUSTED_PROXIES` (comma-separated CIDRs, empty by default) to the address ARTEX sees the proxy connect from: - **nginx and ARTEX both on the host** (binary, `./start.sh`): the peer is `127.0.0.1`; start ARTEX with `ARTEX_TRUSTED_PROXIES=127.0.0.1/32`. - **nginx on the host, ARTEX in Docker** (`docker-compose.yml`): the connection reaches the container from the Docker bridge gateway (a `172.x` address), not from `127.0.0.1`. Find it with `docker network inspect artex_default --format '{{(index .IPAM.Config 0).Gateway}}'` (the network is `_default`), put `ARTEX_TRUSTED_PROXIES=/32` in `.env`, then `docker compose up -d`. For a peer in that list, ARTEX reads `X-Forwarded-For` from the right and takes the first address that is not a trusted proxy; from any other peer the header is ignored. Trust only proxies you run: a trusted peer can claim any client address. > Only when SSE needs a different origin from the page (e.g. a dedicated subdomain) should you set > `NEXT_PUBLIC_SSE_BASE` **at build time** (it is baked into the static bundle during `next build`; > setting it at container runtime has no effect). --- ## Operations ### Backups `scripts/backup.sh` dumps the Postgres database (and optionally the data directory) with timestamped output and rotation: ```bash scripts/backup.sh --with-data # db dump + data/ archive, keep 14 scripts/backup.sh --keep 7 # db only, keep 7 ``` Restore into a running stack: ```bash gunzip -c backups/artex-db-.sql.gz | docker compose exec -T postgres \ psql -U "$POSTGRES_USER" -d "$POSTGRES_DB" ``` Stored secrets (LLM API keys and proxies, MCP env, task credentials, notification channel config, Brave/Tavily search keys, web search and global proxies, the execution spec of custom tools) are encrypted in the database with the key in `keys/secret.key` (generated at first start, mode 0600, next to `jwt.key`). **A database backup without that key cannot restore those secrets**: back up `keys/` with the dump, separately. Deployments without a persistent disk set `ARTEX_SECRET_KEY` (32 bytes, base64 or hex, e.g. `openssl rand -base64 32`). ARTEX refuses to start when the database holds encrypted secrets and no key is available. Daily cron example (03:20, operator crontab): ``` 20 3 * * * cd /path/to/ARTEX && scripts/backup.sh --with-data >> backups/backup.log 2>&1 ``` ### Updating and upgrading > Upgrading swaps the program and never touches data: the Postgres volume `pgdata`, `./data` > (traffic index, task files, transcripts), `./keys` (`jwt.key`, `secret.key`) and `./skills` are > preserved. **No manual database step is needed**: on every start ARTEX applies its embedded > `schema.sql` baseline, then any pending numbered migration from `db/migrations/`, in order, each > in its own transaction. Restarting the new binary is the upgrade. Back up `./data`, `keys/` and > the database before upgrading. **Update banner (opt-in, off by default)**: start ARTEX with `ARTEX_UPDATE_CHECK=1` to ask the public GitHub releases API for the latest tag, at most once per 24 hours (cached in memory; a failed check is not retried within that window). When the release is newer, the web UI shows a dismissible strip linking to Releases. The request sends only `User-Agent: artex-update-check`. Unset, ARTEX makes no update request and shows no banner. #### Upgrading from a clone made before 2026-10-23 The repository history was rewritten that day to drop a personal email address from the commit metadata. A clone made before then cannot fast-forward, and `./update.sh` now stops instead of silently rebuilding stale code. Recover once, then upgrade normally: ```bash git stash # only if you have local changes git fetch origin git reset --hard origin/main git stash pop # only if you stashed ``` Your data is unaffected: `./data`, the `pgdata` volume and `./skills` are not part of git history. #### Option 1: one-click update script ```bash cd ARTEX ./update.sh ``` The script optionally `git pull`s, then offers **① Docker update** (`docker compose build artex` → `docker compose up -d artex`) or **② local build update** (rebuild the frontend static assets, then recompile `./artex`; restart the process for it to take effect). #### Option 2: Docker Compose (manual) ```bash cd ARTEX git pull docker compose build artex docker compose up -d artex docker image prune -f # optional ``` #### Option 3: prebuilt binaries Download the new zip, stop the old process, overwrite `artex` and `skills/` (keep `config.json` and `data/`), then restart: ```bash cp -r /skills ./ && cp /artex ./ ./start.sh ``` #### Option 4: build from source ```bash git pull cd web && npm ci && npm run build:static && cd .. cp -r web/out server/webui/dist CGO_ENABLED=0 go build -tags embedui -o artex ./cmd/artex # restart ./start.sh ``` --- ## Development ```bash ./dev.sh # backend(:8787) + traffic proxy(:8788) + frontend next dev(:5173) → http://localhost:5173 ``` - Backend: `go run ./cmd/artex` (without `-tags embedui`, the frontend is not embedded) - Frontend: `cd web && npm run dev` (`/api` is reverse-proxied to the backend, with hot reload) - Tests: `go test ./...` - Mock preview (no backend): `cd web && NEXT_PUBLIC_MOCK=1 npm run dev` --- ## Architecture ARTEX is an **LLM multi-agent-driven autonomous penetration testing system**: a Go monolithic backend (with the Next.js UI embedded) + PostgreSQL. Agent capabilities come from the [`norma`](https://github.com/Autumn-27/norma) SDK (`agentcore` / `tool` / `permission` / `harness` / `memory` / `transcript`). At its core is the **dual-graph architecture**, plus two autonomy mechanisms: **process-level information exchange between workers** and the **planner's multi-round shared todolist**. ```mermaid flowchart TB subgraph FE["Frontend Next.js (go:embed embedded single binary)"] UI["Dashboard · Tasks · Assets · Coverage graph · Traffic · Workspace · System settings"] end subgraph SRV["server (Go net/http)"] API["REST /api/* JWT auth SSE"] ENG["engine scheduling loop"] MGR["Manager task/engine/store lifecycle"] end subgraph AG["agent (norma SDK)"] GO["goals goal decomposition + scope extraction"] PL["planner the planner (sole intent generator)"] WK["worker executor ×N"] MA["mainagent human-in-the-loop"] end subgraph DB["PostgreSQL"] AGRAPH["Asset graph assets / companies / task_scope"] EGRAPH["Exploration graph exploration_nodes / anchors / activity"] end subgraph SUB["Supporting subsystems"] PROXY["Traffic recording proxy MITM + CA tracing"] GUARD["guard / intercept tool approval gate"] ENR["enrich DNS / HTTP async enrichment"] EXT["MCP · skills · memory · report"] end UI -->|HTTP| API API --> MGR --> ENG ENG --> PL ENG --> WK API --> MA API --> GO PL --> DB WK --> DB MA --> DB GO --> DB WK -->|"Bash / HTTP fully traced"| PROXY WK --> GUARD WK --> ENR PL -.-> EXT WK -.-> EXT MA -.-> EXT ``` | Layer | Responsibility | | --- | --- | | **Frontend** | Next.js static export embedded via `go:embed`; tasks, assets, exploration and coverage graphs, traffic, human-in-the-loop chat | | **server** | `net/http` routing, JWT auth, SSE; `Manager` owns tasks, engines and DB stores | | **engine** | One `plannerLoop` + N worker goroutines per task; intent claiming, timeout/pause/drain | | **agent** | goals / planner / worker / mainagent; `ToolSet` exposes the dual graphs as LLM tools | | **db** | PostgreSQL persistence (pgx); embedded schema and numbered migrations applied at startup | | **Supporting** | Recording MITM proxy, approval gate, async enrichment, MCP/skills/memory/report | --- ## Security Please report vulnerabilities privately through GitHub Security Advisories; see [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md). Operational security properties: - **Secrets at rest**: LLM keys/proxies, MCP environment, task credentials, notification config, search keys, proxies, custom-tool execution specs and traffic evidence snapshots are encrypted with AES-256-GCM using `keys/secret.key` (or `ARTEX_SECRET_KEY`). ARTEX refuses to start when encrypted data exists and no usable key is available. - **First-run claim**: `/setup` requires a one-time token printed at startup; the UI binds to `127.0.0.1` by default. - **Login protection**: 10 attempts per minute per client IP, with `ARTEX_TRUSTED_PROXIES` for correct client attribution behind a reverse proxy. - **Untrusted tool output**: framed as data for every agent by default (prompt-injection boundary). - **Release integrity**: SHA-256 sums, CycloneDX SBOM and GitHub build provenance attestations for release archives. --- ## About this fork This repository is the English translation and continuation of ARTEX, originally by [Autumn-27](https://github.com/Autumn-27).
